newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to sell 13.3 mln Korea Telecom shrs in Nov.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to sell 13.3 mln Korea Telecom shrs in Nov.

text.p: South Korea's Finance Ministry said on Wednesday it will sell 13.3 million shares of Korea Telecom, valued at 500 billion won, in November.
The sale represents 4.6 percent of the state-backed telephone service provider, the ministry said in a statement.
The minimum bid for the shares was set at 37,600 won per share, the statement said.
An additional 3.32 million shares would be sold to Korea Telecom employees.
Bidding is scheduled for November 11-12, and successful buyers will be notified on November 16, it said.
Institutional investors and corporations are eligible to participate in the auction, which is being managed by Kookmin Bank.
The ministry said the sale aimed to help increase the government's revenue. Korea Telecom is unlisted but analysts said they believed it could seek listing next year.
Korea Telecom has a monopoly on South Korea's local telephone service, and holds the lion's share of the long distance and data communication markets.
Currently, the government owns about 80 percent of the company.
